title: Compact overview strip, stacked legend behavior, and accessible trimmed-tooltips for time-series
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Design and spec work for a compact overview strip (mini-timeline) and a stacked legend interaction model for dense timeseries views. Add a trimmed-tooltip strategy that summarizes truncated series when visualization decimates or compresses points, and ensure full keyboard/AT support with ARIA snapshots for dynamic summaries. Goal: keep high-density dashboards usable at small heights while maintaining accessibility and measurable latency improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Compact overview strip implemented as a token-driven component usable across dashboard cards
Legend supports stacking/collapsing per-group with keyboard focus, announce state via ARIA live regions
Trimmed-tooltip provides a condensed summary for clipped series and links to a full detail panel on keyboard activation
Performance benchmarks show ≥25% reduction in time-to-interactive on 50-series graphs using canvas tiling and progressive decimation
Design tokens for spacing, focus outlines, and compact typography added to tokens palette
Accessible examples added to the component docs with voiceover/JAWS verification notes
decision_summary: We will adopt an offscreen canvas tiling renderer for high-density charts with an SVG fallback for small-series or editable charts. Legends will move from linear inline lists to a stacked accordion pattern when available vertical space is tight; stack state is keyboard-controllable and announced through an ARIA live region. Tooltips for decimated views will switch to a trimmed-summary mode that shows aggregate metrics (min/median/max, visible percent) and exposes a keyboard-triggered 'Expand details' action that opens the right-hand detail rail. Color and spacing will use existing token names: color-series-*, spacing-compact-*, focus-ring-strong.
notes: Design dev pairing session scheduled 2026-02-18 with eng runtime team to validate offscreen canvas integration
Related infra ticket ENG-48233 for GPU-backed rendering experiment — dependency for larger rollouts
comments: 2026-02-12 — Ava Moreno: Initial problem framing after shadowing support calls where customers found dense dashboards unreadable at 160px height. Proposing compact overview + stacked legend to reclaim vertical space.

2026-02-18 — Riley Chen: Paired with runtime eng. Offscreen canvas approach seems feasible but requires new paint invalidation signals. ENG will prototype a tile-based compositor. Adding ENG-48233 as a dependency.

2026-02-25 — Priya Nair (Accessibility review): Requested ARIA live region for legend state changes, clarified that trimmed-tooltips must expose full text to screenreader on expand. Also recommended announcing summary stats when focus moves into the chart.

2026-03-03 — UX Research: Micro-usability test (n=8) on compact strip showed 82% task success for series selection, but users missed collapsed legend affordance; adding a visible chevron and focus hint.

2026-03-10 — Riley Chen: Perf experiment results: canvas tiling + progressive decimation reduced initial paint by 28% and memory use by ~12% on host VM with 50 series. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-ui/pull/4182

2026-03-12 — Ava Moreno: Updated visuals in Figma based on UX research; final spec ready for dev handoff. Attaching token mapping and accessibility checklist below. Marking as In Progress and targeting console-2026.03 release for initial rollout.
